The dynamic width reference `{}` would try to consume an argument id, but the parse context I create is fresh.

This is the known issue mentioned in the macro comment. Let me check how the range `join_view` handles this. Looking at the format-test.cc line 1615: `EXPECT_EQ("1, 2, 3", fmt::format("{0:{1}}", join(v1, v1 + 3, ", "), 1));` - this works for the range join_view because it uses a single `value_formatter_` that is parsed once with the original parse context (which has access to the args).

For the tuple case, the dynamic width/precision is problematic because we re-parse for each element. However, this is a known limitation. Let me check what the actual fmt library did.

Actually, let me reconsider. The issue is that the dynamic width `{}` in the spec needs to be resolved against the format arguments. When I create a fresh `basic_format_parse_context`, the dynamic width reference is stored as an `arg_ref`, and during `format` it's resolved against the format context's args. But the issue is the arg index/counting.

Wait, let me look more carefully. The `dynamic_specs_handler::on_dynamic_width` calls `context_.check_arg_id(arg_id)` and stores the arg_ref. During format, `handle_dynamic_spec` resolves the arg_ref against the context's args. 

The problem is that the arg_ref index. When the original format string `"{:{}}"` is parsed, the `{1}` (or auto-indexed) refers to the second argument (the width `4`). But when I re-parse just the spec `{}` (the part after `:`), the parse context starts fresh and the dynamic width `{}` would be auto-indexed as argument 0, but argument 0 is the tuple_join_view itself, not the width.

This is a fundamental issue with re-parsing. Let me check how the actual fmt library handles this. 

Actually, let me reconsider the whole approach. The actual fmt library's fix for this issue (PR #2469 by vitaut) took a different approach. Let me look at what they did.

Actually, the cleaner approach that handles dynamic width/precision is to NOT re-parse, but instead store the parsed spec and apply it. But the problem is the tuple elements have different types, so we can't have a single formatter.

Looking at the existing tests, there's no test for dynamic width with tuple join. The format-test.cc line 1615 tests dynamic width with range join (not tuple join).

Let me check what the actual fmt library did. Let me look at the git history of the actual fmt library for this. The fix was in commit that added `FMT_TUPLE_JOIN_SPECIFIERS`. Actually, looking back at my earlier macro-based approach - that was actually closer to what the real fmt library did. The real fmt library added `FMT_TUPLE_JOIN_SPECIFIERS` macro (default 0) precisely because of the dynamic width/precision issue.

Wait, but the PR description wants format specifiers to work. Let me re-read the PR.

The PR says: "When using `fmt::join`, I'd expect the given format specifier to be applied to each element in the tuple."

So the basic case `{:02}` should work. The dynamic width/precision is a more advanced case that may not be expected to work.
